source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master title says Patch Role Collection, but the Procedure performs only a GET on the collection and the Criteria check only readability/success. It defines no member, writable property, value, privilege effect or PATCH acceptance. DeepSeek's RoleId=Administrator is not source authority.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The role-policy domain is identifiable and an owner can correct the exact mutation contract. Execution is prohibited until then, but the missing decisions are explicit project/user prerequisites rather than an irreducible technical blocker.

review_improvement: Records the GET/PATCH and collection/member conflict, rejects the invented Administrator escalation and defines the authorization, concurrency and recovery evidence required for any corrected case.
independent_technical_reasoning: A role PATCH needs a specific mutable member property, known pre-state, approved post-state and expected privilege delta. This row supplies none of them: only its title suggests a write, while the authoritative steps and criteria remain a collection GET. RoleId may be implementation-defined or immutable, so adopting Administrator would both invent intent and risk escalation. Any later approved write must be ETag-protected and must prove that recovery/operator access survives before rollback is considered safe.
